summary: Christian-Friedrich von Graefe was a linguist who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Leipzig (1796–1805). He held chairs in Greek and Latin at the Main Pedagogical Institute, served as Conservator and Honorary Director at the State Hermitage Museum, and joined the Russian Academy of Sciences.

Christiane Papa-Kalantari is a scholar in history, archaeology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. After a voluntariat at the Austrian National Library in 1998 and a fellowship at the University of Vienna (2003–2006), she became an FWF project director and postdoctoral researcher at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (2025).

Christiane Strothmann works in Tibetology and other fields. She was an Artist in Progress (2016–2018) and lecturer (2024–2026) at Folkwang University of the Arts, as well as a lecturer at the University of Paderborn (2023–2026).

Linguist and Indologist Christianus Cornelis Uhlenbeck studied under Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern and Pieter Jacob Cosijn at Leiden University (Ph.D. 1888). He served as professor of Sanskrit at the University of Amsterdam (1892–1899) and professor of Old Germanic languages and comparative linguistics at Leiden (1899–1926).

Christine Chojnacki is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who completed her doctoral thesis at Sorbonne Nouvelle University in 1991. She is attested as a professor at Jean Moulin University Lyon 3 in 2018.
Indologist Christine Henriëtte Raabe earned her Ph.D. from Utrecht University (~1900–1911), where she studied under Johan Hendrik Gallée and doctoral supervisor Willem Caland.

Christine Mollier works in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, having studied under Kristofer Schipper and Michel Soymié. She served as a researcher and Director of Research at the CNRS, and as Numata Visiting Professor of Buddhist Studies at the University of Chicago.

Christmas Humphreys was a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar who studied at Malvern College and Trinity Hall. He founded the Buddhist Society in 1924 and served as its president until 1983.

Christof Zotter is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. Attested in 2018, he has served as a postdoctoral researcher and head of the editorial program at the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities, and as an editorial board member for Documenta Nepalica.

Christoph Anderl is a scholar in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He completed his MA at the University of Vienna and earned his PhD at the University of Oslo (1997–2004) under Christoph Harbsmeier, later joining Ghent University as a permanent member around 2012.

Christoph Cüppers is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen, Srinivasa Ayya Srinivasan, and Albrecht Wezler. Around 1993, he became the Director of the Lumbini International Research Institute.

Christoph Emmrich works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, holding doctorates from the Free University of Berlin, University of Tübingen, and Heidelberg University under Axel Michaels. He has taught at Heidelberg, the University of Toronto, and the University of Chicago as Numata Visiting Professor.

Sinologist and linguist Christoph Harbsmeier studied at Merton College, Oxford, and completed his Ph.D. at the University of Copenhagen (1981). He taught at Universiti Sains Malaysia, became a professor at the University of Oslo in 1980, and held advisory professorships across China.

Christoph Kleine, a scholar of religion, Japanology, and Buddhist studies, completed his degrees and habilitation at the University of Marburg. He held professorships in East Asian religion and philosophy at the University of Munich (2004–2008) and history of religion at the University of Leipzig (from 2008).
Christoph Theodosius Walther was an Indologist and linguist who studied theology at the University of Halle in 1720. He served as a missionary with the Danish-Halle Mission from around 1725 to 1740.

Anthropologist and Indologist Christoph von Fürer-Haimendorf studied at the University of Vienna and the London School of Economics under Bronisław Malinowski. He was a professor at Osmania University (1945–1949) before serving as Chair of Asian Anthropology at the University of London (1951–1976).

Christoph-Ernst Hauri was a linguist and Indologist who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Basel (1960). He held teaching posts at the universities of Geneva, Lausanne, Texas Health Science Center, and Queensland, and was Titularprofessor of linguistics at the University of Zurich (1988–1995).

Indologist Christophe Jaffrelot completed his education at Sciences Po under Jean Leca by 1991. He has held long-term posts at the CNRS and Sciences Po, and was appointed Professor of Indian Politics and Sociology at King's College London around 2012.

Christophe Vielle is an Indologist who has served as a professor and research professor at the Université catholique de Louvain. His career also includes attested affiliations with institutions such as Leiden University, Columbia University, the Russian Academy of Sciences, and Ghent University.

Christopher Andreas Holmboe was a Norwegian scholar of linguistics, history, archaeology, and Indology. After studying at the University of Oslo and in Paris under Silvestre de Sacy and Caussin de Perceval, he served as professor of Oriental languages at Oslo from 1825 to 1876.
